newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cable TV seen in 23.8 pct of cabled homes.
newsitem.headline: French cable TV seen in 23.8 pct of cabled homes.

text.p: Cable television is watched in 23.8 percent of the homes in France that are equipped to receive cable TV, a figure that has increased in the last two years, according to Mediametrie, an audience measurement body.
The Audicable study published this week and carried out in January said 3.81 million viewers in France aged four and over received basic cable TV service.
The last time the study was carried out, in December 1995, 20.1 percent of "cabled" homes subscribed to basic cable service, Mediametrie said in a statement.
The share of terrestrial television channels in France fell to 76.2 percent in January 1997 from 79.9 percent in December 1995, it said.

So-called "theme channels" took 13.4 percent of France's potential TV audience in January 1997 compared with 12.3 percent in December 1995, general interest channels took 8.3 percent compared with 6.1 percent, while foreign channels took an unchanged 1.3 percent. Other channels accounted for 0.4 percent.

The most watched channels were RTL9 with 2.40 million viewers, sports channel Eurosport with 1.54 million, TMC channel with 1.30 million, documentary channel Planete 1.23 million, music channel MCM with 1.05 million, children's channel Canal J with 1.03 million and LCI channel with 1.00 million viewers.
Mediametrie said most of the channels in the study were also available on satellite services, but the Audicable study did not measure satellite audiences.
